sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Rakesh Kumar Rathore,Sanjeev Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
Heard Sri Rakesh Kumar Rathore, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.P. Patel, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.

2. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 667 of 2018, under Sections 364, 342 & 420 of IPC, Police Station Kotwali, District Mainpuri, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

3. As per prosecution story, the co-accused persons, Ashu Tomar, Dinesh, Bhanu Pratap and Annu are stated to have abducted the husband of the informant as he had gone for execution of a sale-deed to the Office of Registrar, Mainpuri on 12.06.2018.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that he is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has apprehension of his arrest.

He has nothing to do with the said Ankit Mishra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194666189/
1 offence as alleged by the prosecution.

sentences.text: Learned counsel has further stated that he is not named in the FIR.
His name has come up later on in the statement of one of the witness Arvind.

Learned counsel has argued that had the applicant committed the said offence, his name would have come up at the time of institution of the FIR as the name of the said witness has been mentioned in the FIR itself.
5. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicant has previous no criminal history except three cases instituted subsequent to the present FIR.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

6. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

7. Considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98", the applicant is entitled to be granted anticipatory bail in this case.

sentences.text: 8. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
